newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen edges up to end higher on JGB gains.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen edges up to end higher on JGB gains.

text.p: June 17 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (Z) 99.13 99.09

The benchmark three-month December Euroyen futures contract edged up to settle higher on Tuesday in quiet trade, with upward moves powered mainly by gains in Japanese government bonds (JGBs), traders said.
An easing of the dollar against the yen and slightly weaker stocks also contributed to the rise, they added.
Key December ended at 99.13, the high for the day, up 0.4 from Monday's settlement, with volume of 35,573 contracts.
The key September 10-year JGB futures contract ended sharply higher after breaking above a key technical point of 124.20 and eventually forging as high as 124.34.

The rise had been triggered by buying of long-term cash bonds by corporate pension funds and public funds during morning trade. More gains were made in late trade as operators rushed to take new long positions after the contract broke above 124.20, bond traders said.
Euroyen futures were dragged higher by this amid an absence of other fresh factors. But traders said a further rise from this level up is likely to be limited.
"Given current conditions, unless factors emerge suggesting bearish economic sentiment, the key Euroyen futures contract is unlikely to rise much above 99.15," one city bank trader said.

The dollar briefly slid as low as 112.98 yen, while the Nikkei closed down by 87.41, at 20,593.66. This helped keep the downside solid but did not provide much actual buying impetus, traders said. A fairly large volume of bids just under 99.09 is expected to keep the downside solid.
Wait-and-see sentiment ahead of the Bank of Japan (BOJ) tankan survey due out June 25 also helped inhibit moves, with the market also waiting for Japan May trade data on Wednesday.

Strong growth in the key trade surplus with the United States could provoke dips in the dollar and Japanese stocks, potentially boosting Euroyen futures. But dealers cautioned that moves could be limited by operator reluctance to take on much in the way of new positions ahead of the tankan.
The overall surplus, due out at 0850 a.m. on Wednesday (2350 GMT Tuesday) is forecast by economists to rise to 548.5 billion yen from 229 billion yen a year earlier.
Market speculation is spreading that the results of the tankan will show poor sentiment. But this is partly factored in, making the overall impact hard to predict, traders said.
Forecasts for the key diffusion index (DI) for manufacturers by economists who were polled by Reuters averaged about zero, but ranged from minus four to plus four.
That compared to plus two in March, when the last survey was conducted and when the tankan forecast a manufacturers' DI of minus one in June.

Overnight call money was traded at 0.51 percent, a rise from Monday's 0.49 percent. Money traders said strong fund-raising demand ahead of bonus payments and continuing rollover of a large amount of certificates of deposit (CDs) helped the rate move higher.
The central bank injected 100 billion yen into the market in the face of a net shortage of 110 billion yen.
Since the overnight rate was well-bid prior to the 0020 GMT operation, some in the market had expected a generous rather than neutral operation, a trust bank trader said.
"But based on previous times, I'd say the BOJ may let the overnight rate rise as far as 0.52 percent before it starts generous operations again," he added.
Around 50 billion yen of three-month CDs were issued at 0.59 percent. CDs were last issued on Friday at the same rate.
--Elaine Lies in Tokyo +81-3-3432-8806
